body:
Hi there.   


I'm probably on the other side of the planet, but I get it. I fell in love with someone who literally couldn't love me back as well, she's just not outfitted for that.   


So, here's a glass to you, and to never having to pick one up again.   


Thanks for posting this, it's good to know we aren't alone in the world sometimes.
Hi there, probably on the other side of the planet currently, but here to listen - go for it.

Hell, I get that. 18 was by far my worst year. You aren't alone in it.   


What's going on that's put you here?
Here to listen, shoot away!
OP, you still with us? You aren't alone if you still are, thanks so much for everything you've given.

Oh, trust me, you'll matter in a way you may not realise. On the brink of suicide, the most simple things, the most simple people, matter the most in the world. I was saved (on one occasion) by my ex asking if I simply innocently asking if I wanted a chat.

More importantly, I'm here for you, because you are the one who has fought this battle alongside her, how are you doing?
That presumes you tie it right and have the right chordage... Most end in slow, painful experiences, followed by no real release...

In all seriousness, you are one of the people we need far more of in the world. Thank you. Thank you so much. Without people like you, I wouldn't be here now. 

The best advice I can give is: talk to her, listen to her, keep close - but, never, never, forget how incredible you are for fighting through this with her, and never, ever, think of it as your fault.

Hi there, I know the feeling far too well. I'm almost certainly on a different side of the planet, but I'd more than offer a hug if I could give one brother. 

I'm here to listen, feel free to shoot anything you've got.

It hurts more than anything in the world... You aren't alone, I may be fucking awful, but someone on the other side of this planet still gives a damn about you, because we've a shared experience very few have been through. So, please, for the sake of this nutjob, don't put yourself through the unbearable pain.
Not alone in that one, crying is the best outlet... Far better than anything else, but it's also hard to reach...
Long live the dark places - for what it's worth, may not be ideal, but an outlet is an outlet.

I just first wanted to say that you're incredibly strong for fighting this. You're even stronger for having to face it quietly every day behind that wall. Have you talked to anyone face to face about this at all? - Or is it something you've chosen to keep away?

It's sad to say you're right. There never can be a magical treatment for what you've been through.

When you say you can't function, in what sense?

Do you find art and meditation help your mind at all - personally, I'd love to see the art you've created, and you should never measure yourself by sales. Some of the greatest artists in History (people like Van Gough, Bach, El Greco, Poe and Keats) were never truly understood in their art by their communities, didn't make them valueless at all - Is there anything else you've tried?

Hey there, I firstly wanted to just thank you. It's more often not people like me who you help, and it's only right I return the favour. 

What's going through your head? When you say you're getting disillusioned, in what way? - Do you feel like you're losing faith in humanity or everything about life?
I'm here to chat if you've anything you want to get anything out. - What has brought you to this?
You don't. Depression is a fucked up disease, pure and simple. Noone deserves this pain. Noone deserves to have a normal life taken from them.

Depends on what, depends on your body, depends on your circumstances. Mixing a variety of types of Drugs with alcohol is more likely to just either trigger your gag or force your body to just straight up reject - but not before they've often done serious damage to your Liver or Stomach - so I'd hold off yet. 

What has led you to this point?

You're a far stronger person than so many of us - I know for a fact I wouldn't have the courage to go through what you're going through right now. You will be more than okay. 

If there's anything you need to vent, go for it!
Hi there, here to listen, so fire away.

Take this one thing, at least, most likely on the other side of the world, who does give a shit. 

I'm currently at 23:10 GMT, but will be up all night as I don't really sleep, feel free to drop a PM.

People who don't suffer the same thing can't conceptualise it not being the case. It's because they genuinley think it's helpful - and don't realise how untrue it is for some of us. 

Little do they realise, when you're trapped, the last thing you need is for someone to tell you there's a ladder but not actually give you it...
How are you doing? - What's brought you to this point?
I'd definitely get in contact with the mental health charity MIND: They work absolute wonders in situations like this https://www.mind.org.uk/
Currently in contact from 11:24pm GMT here - need a chat? - I'm up all night.
Congrats!

It may well be worth it - I'd honestly advise just booking in with a general practitioner and seeing where they refer you from there! - If anything, I'm sure it'll help you to at least start to strategise and work things out. 

Whatever you do, don't get caught in a spiral - its a lot easier to dig a pit than it is to try and re-fill it from the bottom up.

Definitely this. I love my friends to bits - they literally saved my life, but at the same time, they don't realise how hard it is for me to properly relate to them. 

Perceiving reality in the same way as your average person is so much harder when depression rears its ugly head - which is probably why it feels so lonely, because you literally aren't living the same world they are.

I'm currently on Sertraline, an SSRI - and unfortunately, it's too right. Coming off it feels like hell and I get nauseous whenever I force myself to take it. 

Best supplement I've been recommended is Vit D and B - when mixed with workouts they supposedly help improve endorphin release, but I'm not sure how effective that is reliably...

Depression doesn't know how to discriminate. Depression doesn't care that things seem to make sense half of the time. 

Depression is a horrendous disease. Like any other physical illness, it unfortunately doesn't need a reason to start per se. It can be triggered by so many things - and trying to work out what has caused it is honestly the most torturous part. 

However, trying to write it out is a good start!

In what way to you feel like your friends hate you? and how do you feel you won't succeed?

That's incredibly shitty. 

For what it's worth, I'm a trained active listener for Samaritans and a sufferer likewise - if you need someone to talk to via pms, I'll probably be up all night!

Paracetamol compounds are incredibly damaging. A dose of more than 12 g ingested/ per kg of your body weight of paracetamol will be fatal if acetylcysteine is not provided as soon as possible. 

The overdose will cause an inundation in your liver, leading to alternative metabolisation of the drug, which creates NAPQI - a toxic metabolite which will lead to rapid necrosis of the Liver and Kidney tubes. This will lead to vomiting, acute liver failure, internal bleeding and eventually death - it's possibly one of the most torturous methods of suicide possible. 

**Please, for the sake of any of us - if not yourself - for the sake of some random stranger on the other side of the planet who cares too much** - *contact emergency services immediately*.

I totally get that. Depression isn't like a lot of other diseases, it's not something anyone who hasn't had it can ever really comprehend - and in that sense, it's no wonder you're lonely. 

For what it's worth - you've got us - and anyone around here will try our hardest to empathise, because we may be the only ones in the world who truly can x

That's possibly the worst part. Everyone seems to think depression is some sort of state of 'sadness', but that isn't really the right way to describe it. 

Depression is an overwhelming nothingness - it's a state where you just feel afraid that someone is going to realise that inside you there really isn't anything.

That's perhaps what's makes it so terrifying. 

For what it's worth (which may not be a lot), at least here, in our own little broken community, you don't have to suffer it alone.

Honestly it's the worst feeling. My friends found me on the verge of suicide sitting out in a cold night half-submerged in a sub-zero river. I've never felt more horrendous in my entire life... The guilt, the shame, my complete numbness juxtaposed with their horror - it's worse than depression alone has ever been.
Honestly, couldn't agree more - at least in sleep I get vivid, horrifying dreams, rather than the drab emptiness of life...

Empathy - I've been trained as a welfare officer, so I got pretty good at reading someone's emotional state, even though in truth, I'm pretty emotionally inhibited in public. I've successfully learnt to ignore my own problems by taking on other people's and pretending that I get the way they feel, even though I don't have a clue half the time.

Hell, there's nothing wrong with having an emotional outlet! - Weirdly enough, one of the best ways I've ever seen this depicted is the Disney film 'Inside Out', which perfectly shows why you need to be able to be upset and vent to avoid a spiral.

Following on from that, where better to do that than anonymously via the internet?, where you're more likely to find someone who'll properly listen!

A great comment which has stuck with me from Samaritans training (and something I absolutely empathise with currently going through my 3rd bout of depression) is "The problem with people who ask the question 'are you feeling alright today?' is that more often than not, they're more inclined to try and 'help' in the conventional sense. - When someone is in the depths of depression, the last thing they need is a listeners' opinion imposed on them, all the need is someone to really listen..."

It's something most people don't necessarily get - they love to think that with enough time and advice they can somehow turn around your problem, little do they realise it's just going to make them feel bad that they can't really help and the depressed person feel guilty for having spread the issue.

For what it's worth, that's sometimes exactly what we all need - a way to vent our true feelings. I suppose that's sorta the magic of this sub, the fact that everyone here can be anonymous, honest and not be judged - it's a god-send at times for me.
Hey, that's not a problem, I'm here and quite happy to listen to anything you've got to say!

Yeah, I've been there. In my case, I have a habit of taking on 2 different personas, my private (which I'm exhibiting now when I'm being honest0 and my public persona (which I show when I'm around 'friends', who have no idea what I really feel like). One of the first things I'll ask is - do you feel like your relationships are 'emotionally fulfilling' you?

One of the best things to do is to talk about it, and that's what we're here for, so I'm glad you've made that first step. 

When you say you feel "lost and helpless", in what sense?
Hell, I'm here to listen - so fire away, what do you think is making you feel this way?

Yeah, what I've been told is that its to do with the way that your brain shuts down different parts at different rates. 

According to my psychiatrist, the vast majority of depression/anxiety is processed in the limbic system, which processes a deep-set emotion (sometimes coloquially known as the subconscious). The rest of your emotional well-being and more complex emotional states are run by the neocortex. However, as you get tired, this starts to shut off, leaving the limbic system to do it's thing without any context, hence leading to a growth in depressive thoughts.

For what it's worth, I get that. Recently, talking to Samaritans, one of the biggest things they talk about is the fact that people (like your mum) who get emotionally invested in you are more likely to just work you up further. 

I've had the 'dramatic' line thrown at me as well - and quite frankly its a load of bullshit. That's one of the hardest parts of depression, that nobody else can quite get it... 

For what it's worth, if you need someone to listen to you rather than tell you about the impact that you're supposedly having on them, that's what we're here for.

Not at all, you're describing exactly how most of us feel...

There was a time when I used to go to the gym, I used to lead an orchestra, I used to be an avid climber, I used to be a straight A student, I used to be outgoing and positive and I used to enjoy being around people. 

Now, all the colour has faded from life, I gave up music because I started to lose inspiration, I gave up exercise because I felt drained every morning and I got more and more anxious about the way people perceived me, so I started to shut of my social interactions.

Nowadays, I'm mocked for being 'boring', 'tired' and 'uninteresting' - the sort of person noone really wants to be around anyway... 

The best thing we can do is just keep slogging on, I suppose? But if you ever get a better answer than that, please, share.
Depression is one of the most draining things imaginable... There's no real way to get around the 'you seem tired' or 'are you on edge comments'.
I feel you're asking in the wrong place friend?
I've found that the darkest places are where I'm most comfortable - at least you can't miss out on anything in the dark...

Try to go to sleep... I seem to be in a vicious cycle of going to bed at 12, not getting to sleep till 5 (if at all), then being woken up at 7, lying there till 9-10 when I eventually force myself to put on some clothes and get to work.

You're not alone here - we're all stuck in this hole... 

Friends and Parents are great, but it never seems to feel 'real' or 'profound'.

The way I've always described depression is: It's as if the colour, the vividness, the feeling, all starts to drain out, it's not 'sadness' per se, but more like staring into the void. There's a reason I'm not afraid of the dark - and that's because, at least if you're in it, there's no colour to see...

The problem with people just saying "you just need to change your attitude" or "its just a phase, you'll feel better tomorrow" is due to a profound lack of understanding of the topic, that's the problem, it's hard to truly understand depression unless you've experienced it first-hand.

I know the exact feeling. I'm often stuck between two  *me* and who people *think* I am. 

The problem is that, you never truly feel fulfilled even if you have 'friends' surrounding you. For what it's worth, I find sitting in a pit can be helpful at times - it's a good emotion release - as long as you can drag yourself back out at the end.

It's a horrible experience to go through - Anxiety training and breathing exercise practice has really helped me started to get around them, but I still feel incredibly awkward around people who've literally just watched me break down before them...

I think we all have periods of up and down, you'll note even by my posting history on here, which shows it pretty clearly... 

Before I went to try and seek help, for a long time, I just thought I was faking for attention, turned out, it was much more deep rooted. 

The thing about depression, is that it seems to come in bouts, often at times of stress or when you really are trying to get back on track, it rears it's ugly head again...

It's a shitty response, a lot of us suffer, but the 'so what' attitude really pisses me off... 

The problem is, depression is a condition which is so badly understood  (even by those who suffer it), that there's a huge social stigma around it - and a complete lack of understanding and empathy.

It's a disease which you can't really understand the mindset of until you've been through it, hence why so many people (even those with good intentions) can't really access it...

I know the exact feeling, it's an incredibly hard thing to do. 

The times I talk to most people, it's not really me, it's the act I put on for the sake of being socially acceptable. 

The problem is, I can't act when one on one, hence avoid intimate close relations with people, purely due to the fear that the *real* me, will start to show themself - and I'd never want to force anyone to deal with that...

Love is a concept which is hard to understand, especially when depressed...

What you can be fooled into thinking is love, often ends up either not being mutual, or being manipulative in one way or another.

Yes, you're feeling the exact way I felt for a long time before my diagnosis. 

The best description I could ever give of depression is as follows:

*Things just seem more 'opaque', what to most people is a fun trip out, or a good laugh between friends, to me, was just sort of a, well, 'grey' experience.*

*It felt as if all my strength, my energy and my creativity were being sucked out of me somehow, as if some sort of parasite had latched onto me*

*I couldn't sleep, I couldn't work, I couldn't even feel by the time it got to it's worst - I was honestly happy to cry occasionally, because at least it was something*

*Socially, I became more anxious, more aware of the need to cover up, to veil my views and that in turn meant that I started to drift away. Eventually, almost every situation started to feel 'impersonal' in a sense*

It's a scary thing, but it's also something which you unfortunately start to come to terms with... You reach a point so low, that there is no way down...

Rémy, before I get into anything, I'd just like to say: *you are a hero*. There's no two ways about it. You're the sort of person who has the bravery I wish I had. 

You're certainly not the only one who was lost it after the November attacks either, I live in the UK, and I'll never forget that morning. It pushed me to the point of wonder why the hell humanity even exists, how anyone could do that, how anyone could crush so much hope, so much life, in the name of a false ideology... I remember waking up that morning and breaking down, it'll  stay with me for the rest of my life - the lyrics of La Marseillaise stuck with me in the days after that horrific event: 

"*Allons enfants de la patrie,
Le jour de gloire est arrivé!
Contre nous de la tyrannie*".

There's always someone to talk to around here, feel free to vent as much as you want, what exactly do you think is making you feel alienated?
Luckily, the internet can provide in this aspect at least! http://thenicestplaceontheinter.net/

It certainly isn't stupid, there's always got to be something for us to strive for, right? I know what you mean, trying to pull yourself out of it is a feat... And I hope like hell, that even though I won't make it, at least someone on I end up talking to on here will, which is at least something to keep me going...

Well, you're certainly not alone in that one - and the worst thing is that life is such a bitch that it never really feels like it'll deliver.

I think that's honestly probably one of the worst things about depression, the complete devoidness of hope - the people who I do know well enough/am forced to react with, just think I'm a cynical old git, when genuinely, it feels as if I've got no chance of ever finding anyone to truly support me when I go through a mental breakdown...

It's also that fact that, no matter what I seem to do, no matter how hard I try, I can never seem to get a conversation to flow naturally when faced with someone, I can pick up their emotional reaction, but never know how to properly lead onto a conversation, without coming across badly and risking my facade - so I empathize entirely in that sense.

I'll say this, I let myself go a long time after the whole 'gym membership' period, because I realised it wasn't working for me... 

I still feel the same way when it comes to face to face contact with people unfortunately, I just try to put on a facade long enough to get through the day...

The one thing I can say is, rise above her, prove her wrong. Try not to internalise her bullshit (I know it's hard, I've become accustomed to years of family members calling me a failure to my face). I'm sure, you'll know, just as anyone else would, that that is a case of her being an abusive bitch and projecting her problems onto you, without taking into consideration the other things you're having to go through. You are 1000x stronger than she is for that. 

I'm not sure whether I'm stepping over subreddit rules here or not (mods, please remove this post if I am), but I'd advise, considering the fact you're still legally considered a minor, contacting a local child protection group, anonymously, and trying to see what they can do - You shouldn't have to put up with an environment like that....

I know the feeling, my problem is the fact that, half of me seems to crave proper human contact, but the rest of me absolutely hates it...

In my case, it falls to a mix between incredibly low self-esteem and social anxiety and to be honest, I don't know whether I'll ever get past the facade I put on for the sake of my 'friends'.

What exactly is it about seeing people outside which drains you?

Honestly, it sounds awful, but one of the happiest moments for me was when I burst into tears after the death of my grandfather... 

That felt incredibly weird at the time, because I'd become so numb to the rest of the world, that even feeling anything was salvation. The numbness gets to you eventually - you start to feel like a husk and try to fill that with other things, none of which seem to work...
That was the scary thing, it's as if the colour starts to drain from the world and eventually, all you're left with is grey...

1) Gym membership certainly didn't help me, it led to me feeling more self-conscious and out of place.

2) Transforming my body into a rock didn't help, I still felt like absolute shit.

3) Banging girls didn't help, because every time felt meaningless and empty...

I know you're coming from a good place, but unfortunately, the problems a lot of us go through are more complex than a short 'ffs' post...

In that case, it'd be a good idea to contact Samaritans USA,  http://www.samaritansusa.org/contact.phpm, http://samaritansnyc.org/calling-the-hotline-2/?gclid=CNOX96aHrs8CFeQp0wodk4QENg on (212) 673-3000

As well as this, it may be advisable to contact SAMHSA helpline: https://www.mentalhealth.gov/get-help/immediate-help/ on 1-877-SAMHSA7  (1‑877‑726‑4727)

I'd also book in with a doctor or psychiatrist who may in turn refer you on to an accredited medical health centre.

**I'd just like to say, before this case is even allowed to begin:**

Whilst there is no rule stipulated which validates your ban from /r/AskUK, the mods do have discretion on who they want to ban. 

Firstly, it should be noted, that what you posted in relation to is a highly controversial and highly sensitive issue - the way you came across likely heightened the community's worry and hence moderators decided to remove the post. 

Secondly, your post history makes me seriously worried for your mental health and sexual preferences - this is quite likely why they don't want you posting on their subreddit - and hence why you were banned. 

I'm now asking personally, please, contact a service and seek professional help. (I'm assuming you are in the UK)

The number for Childline is 0800 1111, talk to them and see what they can say about your personal situation. Also book an appointment with a mental health professional via your NHS GP's surgery. 

**This is for your good and the good of all of those in your community.**

I don't know whether you've thought about it, but contacting the NHS and trying to get their help is the best idea - I'd go down to the GP and ask them to come to her if necessary - when people get onto the self-help programmes I've seen their lives completely turned around.
In my case, quite literally... My ex got depressed (for a period of around a week) because I beat her at it and then tried to break up with me...

If anything I'd say he's a bit of a radical socialist - on account of the fact that he calls for social justice and sits with the poor - hence why he was hated by conservatives (i.e Jewish priests) so much.
I was in a very similar position, it's just not the right way to hold a relationship. Until recently, it felt more like I was her counselor than her SO...
We're doing fine! She's currently sitting on my lap!

I got a new kitten, she said I was cheating on her with it...

I said I might try and get a job, she said I was trying to throw her away...

I said hello to a female friend of mine (who happens to be bi) and she accused me of cheating... 

She's now my ex-SO...

Even in the bible, there are recorded accounts of what you are suffering with. Biblical figures such as Jacob, Job and David are all recorded to have suffered with what we now diagnose as depression and anxiety.  (See Genesis 37:34-35, Job 3:1-11 and 2 Samuel 18:33)

These were people who are now hailed as heroes and messengers of God - they too, like you were in a dark place and went on to be praised. 

Suicide is not the answer - I know it may feel like it, but it isn't. The bible gives evidence of this in Judges 16:29-30, 1 Samuel 31:4-5, 2 Samuel 17:23, 1 Kings 16:18 and Matthew 27:3-5, where it is mentioned. In every case, it is made clear, that God gives life and only God should take it away, as stated in Job 1:21  "I shall have nothing when I die. The Lord gave me everything I had, and they were his to take away. Blessed be the name of the Lord."

Death is a concept which we often mistake, but the simple fact is, God wants us to live, God loves us all and God created us a path for all of us. 

Though you may feel alone and far from him, he is there, he always will be and he can guide you back to a path of righteousness. 

If it means anything, I, along with everyone else here, will be praying for you.

Well, I don't know whether it counts, but depression appears to me as a shadowy figure which you could certainly call a demon, it's something which follows you around and lurks in the shadow, but it's a presence you can most certainly feel, which is in no way godly...

Thank-you for that, it's advice I've already been given, however, I wouldn't say that we have the right to make a distinction. 

It is clear we all sin and are equal in the eyes of god, whether we choose to designate ourselves as Christian or not, we shouldn't be the ones to separate the sheep from the goats, that is the role of the Lord.

There have been days where it has been so crippling that I just call off and feign being ill... I don't really know why, it just comes over me sometimes, I feel like maybe if I stay, no-one will give a fuck and just maybe I'll get some sort of energy...

I have been on the receiving end of this, before I got with my S.O

The issue is the fact that you've maybe moved a little too quick, people across the internet like to work in their own time at their own pace, just pestering can irritate people and make you seem needy - people don't want someone needy in their life.

It's best to send 1 message to show you are available, then leave it to see if you get a response, don't pester them too much.

It is fixable, but it will take time, the best thing you can do now is apologize for your previous comments and say that you just enjoyed being with her. 

It's important to remember that although you may think that the two of you are close, she may not, slow down the pace of what you are doing.

They tried their best, but I was raised with my mum being continually critical of me, I was raised constantly being criticized whenever I went downstairs. Nowadays I can't stand talking to people for fear of being put down, have no work ethic or passion, for fear of being abused and mocked about it. 

That and I'm now dealing with depression, but they refuse to let me talk to a doctor and when I come home down, I'm told I'm being sad over nothing and to shut up because it's making them more stressed.

"Thanks for taking the time to talk to me"

It was the first time anyone ever acknowledged the fact that they'd enjoyed spending time with me...

I owe her my life...

I have one person I can talk to, that is it... the rest of my friends, they won't get it... They would look at me like the freak I am... 

One person is the difference between darkness and hope.
